# Vyre

> Vyre is an open-source, self-hosted home for your AI agents. Agents run on a server you own,
> keep working when your laptop is closed, and answer from your Mac (Option-Space, Vyre Lumen),
> your phone (the web app on your Home Screen) or Windows (a Windows app).

## What it is
One small daemon plus apps around it. It runs Claude (through the Agent SDK), Codex and Grok
(through ACP) and OpenRouter from your own subscriptions. A session belongs to Vyre, not to a model:
you pick the model for each session, or add @codex or @grok to one message, and the session keeps its
memory and files.

## What runs where
- Vyre runs on a server you control: a Linux machine with Docker, or a Mac that stays on.
- The Deck (the web app) is served from your own address, `<you>.vyre.run` or your own domain.
- Vyre Lumen is the Mac app; press Option-Space to reach it. There is a Windows app too (a tray icon
  and an Alt-Space panel).
- Your devices reach your server over Tailscale, which is required (the free plan is enough).

## Set up
Open https://vyre.run/setup. It gives you one line to paste on your server, then walks you through
naming your server, signing in to your AI, connecting Tailscale and adding your phone.

On a Linux server or a Mac that stays on, the line the page shows is:
```
curl -fsSL https://vyre.run/i | VYRE_CODE=<code> sh
```
Without a code, from the terminal only: `curl -fsSL https://vyre.run/install.sh | sh`.
On your Mac, with Tailscale installed and signed in (Node 22.5 or newer):
```
npm install -g https://vyre.run/box/vyre.tgz
vyre up
vyre capsule install
```
`vyre capsule install` builds Vyre Lumen on your Mac; nothing is downloaded for it.

## Cost
Vyre itself is free and open source. You pay your AI providers the way you do today.

## Data
Prompts go to the provider you choose. Keys, memory and sessions stay on your server, and the server
publishes no port to the internet. vyre.run holds your name's DNS record and runs the relay
(relay.vyre.run), which carries setup progress and phone pairing end to end encrypted: it can see that a
server and a device talk, and when, but never what is said or your keys.

## Not in 0.2.0
0.2.1: Touch ID prompts for terminal commands that need them, a Safari fix for interactive artifacts,
Chrome API routing and parallel tabs, "give it to two" and per-provider blocks. 0.2.5: Spaces
(team spaces and sharing), memory rollover, putting idle sessions to sleep.
